Calculate Simpipe P-value Uniformity Distribution Score (Approach 2)

Source: R/05_metrics_de_signal.R
calc_simpipe_distribution_score.Rd

Evaluates the reliability of candidate DEGs returned by simulation methods according to the Simpipe benchmarking framework (Duo et al., Genome Biology 2024).

Usage

calc_simpipe_distribution_score(
  sim_data,
  sim_celltypes,
  candidate_degs = NULL,
  n_bins = 10,
  alpha = 0.05,
  min_cells = 5
)

Arguments

sim_data

Simulated count matrix (genes x cells).

sim_celltypes

Factor or character vector of simulated cell groups.

candidate_degs

Optional list of character vectors of candidate DEGs per pair to remove. If NULL, edgeRQLFDetRate is first run on sim_data to identify candidate DEGs for removal.

n_bins

Number of histogram bins for the Pearson chi-squared goodness-of-fit test (default 10).

alpha

Significance threshold for accepting the uniform null hypothesis (default 0.05). If test p-value > alpha, null is accepted (S = 1).

min_cells

Minimum number of cells per group (default 5).

Value

A list containing:

distribution_score

Overall Simpipe distribution score (0 to 1)

pairwise_results

Data frame with per-pair details: Group1, Group2, N_removed, N_remaining, Chisq_Stat, Chisq_Pval, Accepted_Null, S_i

pvalues_remaining

Named list of P-value vectors for the remaining genes per pair

Details

The hypothesis is that if there are no DEGs between two sample groups, the false positive rate of detected DEGs should be approximately 0.05 and P-values should follow a uniform distribution \(U(0, 1)\). Candidate DEGs returned by the simulation method are directly removed from the simulated gene expression matrix, and differential expression analysis is performed on the remaining genes using edgeRQLFDetRate.

The Pearson chi-squared goodness-of-fit test is performed on the remaining P-values under the null hypothesis of uniformity across 10 equal bins. If the null hypothesis is accepted (\(P > 0.05\)), \(S_i = 1\); otherwise \(S_i = 0\).

For 2 groups (\(n = 2\)): $$\text{distribution score} = 0 \text{ or } 1$$ For 3 or more groups (\(n > 2\)): $$\text{distribution score} = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^N S_i$$ where \(N = \binom{n}{2}\) is the number of paired groups.

Examples

data(example_scrna, package = "scSimEval")
res <- calc_simpipe_distribution_score(
  sim_data = example_scrna$sim,
  sim_celltypes = example_scrna$cell_types
)
#> calcNormFactors has been renamed to normLibSizes
#> calcNormFactors has been renamed to normLibSizes
res$distribution_score
#> [1] 1
